Academic Life

Academic Units of Debre Markos University

Debre Markos University organizes its academic work through colleges, institutions, and schools that support teaching, research, and professional development across a wide range of disciplines.

College

College of DMU

Debre Markos University delivers undergraduate and postgraduate education through a broad set of colleges that support academic excellence, applied research, and community development. These colleges provide the foundation for knowledge creation and professional training in core and emerging disciplines.

Each college brings related fields together so students can build strong subject knowledge and apply it to practical questions. Coursework, projects, and research activities help learners strengthen critical thinking, communication, and problem-solving skills for work and further study.

  • College of Natural and Computational Sciences – offers programs in mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology, computer science, and related technical fields.
  • College of Social Sciences and Humanities – develops learning in language, literature, history, governance, culture, psychology, and social studies.
  • College of Business and Economics – prepares students in accounting, finance, economics, management, and business leadership.
  • College of Agriculture and Natural Resources – supports agricultural development, environmental management, food security, and natural-resource studies.

Institution and School

Institution and School of DMU

DMU also runs specialized institutions focused on applied and technology-based learning. These centers help bridge academic knowledge with practical problem-solving in engineering, land systems, and development planning.

The Institute of Technology connects scientific principles with engineering and technology applications. The Institute of Land Administration focuses on how land information and governance support planning, responsible land use, and public decision-making.

  • Institute of Technology – promotes engineering education, innovation, technology transfer, and applied technical training.
  • Institute of Land Administration – focuses on land governance, geospatial information, surveying, and land-management systems.

Schools

The university's schools provide professional and specialized learning for disciplines that require focused training, practical experience, and high standards of academic preparation.

School-based study emphasizes the knowledge, judgment, and professional responsibility needed in each field. Law education develops legal reasoning and an understanding of justice and governance, while health education prepares learners to contribute to individual and community well-being.

  • School of Law – develops legal literacy, professional ethics, governance understanding, and legal practice capacity.
  • School of Medicine and Health Sciences – trains future health professionals in medicine, public health, nursing, pharmacy, and related fields.
